name: Knock Poker
description: Knock Poker (also known as Rap Poker) is an American draw and discard game in which the aim is to collect the best five-card poker hand. Unlike traditional poker, there is no betting process of raising and folding. Instead, players draw cards from a stock pile or take the previous player's discard, with the ability to 'knock' to end the round when they believe they have the strongest hand.

content.text: Knock Poker (also known as Rap Poker) is an American draw and discard game in which the aim is to collect the best five-card poker hand. Unlike traditional poker, there is no betting process of raising and folding. Instead, players draw cards from a stock pile or take the previous player's discard, with the ability to 'knock' to end the round when they believe they have the strongest hand.

Knock Poker emerged in the United States in the early 20th century as a non-gambling alternative to traditional poker. It was documented in Albert Ostrow's 'The Complete Card Player' (1945) and later in Scarne's 'Encyclopedia of Games' (1973).
3 to 5 players optimal. Can be played with 2 or more than 5 using the same rules.
Poker chips or coins for scoring and a central pot.

Cards are shuffled, cut by the player to dealer's right, and dealt one at a time until each player has five cards. The remainder forms a draw pile, with the top card turned face up to start the discard pile.

items.text: Simple Settlement: Knock ends play immediately with no additional turns. Best hand simply takes the pot with no other payments.
Ante Per Draw: Each player adds an extra chip to the pot each time they draw a card.
Minimum Knock Requirement: Players can only knock with a minimum hand such as a pair of Jacks or a pair of Aces.
Bonus Wins: Extra bonuses paid by all players: 2 chips for knocking on first turn without drawing, 4 chips for royal flush, 2 chips for straight flush, 1 chip for four of a kind.
Dompe: Mexican variant played with a Joker as wild card and possibility of winning with a 6-card hand.
